hero.intro: It's 3 a.m. again. The fix you tried didn't hold, and every free answer contradicts the last one.
hero.description: an answer to your situation, written from a named Stanford scientist's own published sleep research, cited to the study so you can check it — or show your doctor. Calm, confident, done searching. And when the research doesn't cover you yet, it says so honestly instead of guessing.

items.p: You've tried the fix. You've read the contradictory advice. What you're buying is one answer to your situation — written from a named Stanford scientist's own published research — and the calm of being done looking.

items.h: A citation you can show someone.
items.p: Every answer is traceable to the study it came from — not a confident-sounding guess assembled from a hundred web pages. Show it to your spouse, your doctor, anyone who asks how you know. You go to the source.

Sometimes the answer isn't what you hoped for — and sometimes there's no answer yet at all. When the research doesn't cover your question, it tells you exactly that instead of inventing something to please you. That honesty is what makes the rest believable.
